title: Prompts that get usable answers
goal: You will create a context-rich prompt, specify its output format, and refine the response into a usable final draft.
prerequisites: A real message, plan, or document you need help drafting

steps.why: A blank conversation prevents earlier messages from influencing this task.
steps.checkpoint: You should see an empty conversation with a message composer near the bottom.
hint_levels: Look near the top of the left sidebar.
Find the button labeled New chat.
Click New chat in the left sidebar.

steps.action: Type one sentence describing the real result you need.
steps.where: Message composer at the bottom of the conversation.
steps.why: A clear task gives the chatbot a concrete outcome to work toward.
steps.checkpoint: You should see a sentence beginning with an action such as "Draft," "Plan," or "Summarize" in the composer.
hint_levels: Start with what you want produced.
Use an action verb and name the intended result.
Click the message composer and type, for example, "Draft a follow-up email to a customer who missed our meeting."

steps.action: Add the relevant background, audience, purpose, and constraints below your task sentence.
steps.where: Same message composer, on new lines beneath the first sentence.
steps.why: Specific context helps the response fit your real situation instead of relying on guesses.
steps.checkpoint: You should see details labeled "Background," "Audience," "Purpose," and "Constraints" in the composer.
hint_levels: Think about what the chatbot cannot know unless you state it.
Include who this is for, what happened, what success means, and any limits.
Press Shift+Enter for new lines, then type "Background:", "Audience:", "Purpose:", and "Constraints:" with your details.

steps.action: Add instructions for the exact structure, length, and tone of the answer.
steps.where: Message composer, beneath the context details.
steps.why: An explicit format makes the first response easier to use and evaluate.
steps.checkpoint: You should see a line beginning with "Output format:" that names a structure, length, and tone.
hint_levels: Describe what the finished answer should look like.
Specify the sections or layout, a length limit, and the desired voice.
Press Shift+Enter, then type, for example, "Output format: Give me a subject line and a 120-word email in a warm, professional tone."

steps.where: Up-arrow Send button at the right side of the message composer.
steps.why: Sending the combined task, context, and format instructions produces a response you can test against your needs.
steps.checkpoint: Your prompt should appear in the conversation, followed by a chatbot response.
hint_levels: Use the control beside the text you entered.
The Send button is the up-arrow at the right edge of the composer.
Click the up-arrow Send button, or press Enter.

steps.action: Compare the response with every requirement in your prompt.
steps.where: Chatbot response in the main conversation panel and your prompt directly above it.
steps.why: Checking against stated requirements reveals what needs to change in the next draft.
steps.checkpoint: You should be able to point to at least one part that works and one specific part to improve.
hint_levels: Check the answer against your own labels.
Review its accuracy, audience fit, purpose, constraints, structure, length, and tone.
Scroll between your prompt and the response, then identify one successful detail and one missing or weak detail.

steps.action: Type a follow-up instruction naming one specific change for the next draft.
steps.where: Message composer below the chatbot response.
steps.why: A targeted revision request is more reliable than accepting the first draft or asking vaguely for improvement.
steps.checkpoint: You should see a follow-up message that identifies what to keep and exactly what to change.
hint_levels: Focus on the most important weakness you noticed.
Tell the chatbot which useful element to preserve and give a measurable revision.
Click the composer and type, for example, "Keep the friendly opening, but shorten the email to 90 words and make the requested next step explicit."

steps.where: Up-arrow Send button at the right side of the message composer.
steps.why: Continuing in the same conversation lets the chatbot revise the existing draft with your feedback.
steps.checkpoint: A revised response should appear below your follow-up instruction.
hint_levels: Submit the follow-up from the same conversation.
Use the same Send control you used for the original prompt.
Click the up-arrow Send button, or press Enter.

steps.action: Enter and send one final follow-up that fixes the most important remaining issue.
steps.where: Message composer below the revised response, then the up-arrow Send button.
steps.why: A second focused iteration turns the response into a draft that is ready for real use.
steps.checkpoint: The newest response should visibly include your requested correction and match the context and output format from the original prompt.
hint_levels: Inspect the revised answer for the one issue that still limits its usefulness.
Name the remaining problem and state the exact replacement or adjustment you want.
Click the composer, type a precise correction such as "Replace the generic closing with two proposed meeting times," then click the up-arrow Send button or press Enter.
